scope.evidence_basis: Actual author reconstruction: Checked sufficiency for all nonzero pairs and necessity by the particular vector x=-A^{-1}By for each nonzero y. The fixed-y minimum is zero in the z-term precisely at z=0. The main statement includes all matrix sizes, symmetry, the strict-positive definition and the unique minimizer. This is classical, not original.

N-S-main: Expand the square with A symmetric and invertible.
Invert the change of variables and prove both positivity directions.
Identify the unique fixed-y minimum using A>0.
Calculate the scalar model and the invertible-indefinite failure.

N-S-main.objects: Fixed real symmetric blocks A,C and rectangular B; test vectors and a fixed-y minimizer.
N-S-main.domain: p,q are positive integers; every real test vector of the stated sizes is allowed.
N-S-main.fixed_and_variable: A,B,C are arbitrary fixed data; x,y vary and the minimum is in x for each y.
N-S-main.hypotheses: A>0 and symmetry are explicit. Positivity supplies invertibility and a true minimum.
N-S-main.equations: M,S and the minimum value and minimizer are displayed.
N-S-main.quantifiers: For every block choice satisfying the hypotheses and every fixed y.
N-S-main.conclusion: M>0 iff S>0 and the fixed-y minimum is attained uniquely.
N-S-main.status: Known classical criterion, expressly not a new result.
N-S-main.local_definitions: Positive definite is defined in the statement; ordinary transpose and inverse are in the declared baseline.
